assistant.r: Plan your revision a week early. Study in short 25-minute blocks with 5-minute breaks.
Put your phone in another room, clear your desk and work on one thing at a time.
Do the hardest homework first while your mind is fresh, then tick tasks off one by one.
In maths, practise a little every day and always write each step. Check your answer by working backwards.
For science, draw diagrams and explain each idea out loud as if you were the teacher.
Read for 20 minutes a day. Pause after each page and say in one sentence what it was about.
Sleep is when your brain stores what you learned. Aim for a regular bedtime.
Take three slow breaths, then write down what you can control. Talking to a teacher or family member helps too.

scenarios.q: A message says: “You won a phone! Click this link now.” What do you do?
opts: Ignore it and tell an adult
Send it to all your friends
scenarios.why: Surprise prizes are a common trick. Never click unknown links.

scenarios.q: A website asks you to make a password. Which is the safest?
opts: A long mix of words, numbers and symbols
scenarios.why: Long, mixed passwords are much harder to guess.

scenarios.q: Someone you only know online asks where you live. What do you do?
opts: Do not answer and tell a trusted adult
scenarios.why: Never share personal details with people you have not met in real life.

scenarios.q: You are on free public Wi-Fi at a cafe. What is safest?
opts: Avoid logging in to important accounts
Share your password with the cafe
scenarios.why: Public Wi-Fi can be watched. Save important logins for a trusted network.

scenarios.q: A friend wants to post a photo of you that you do not like. What do you do?
opts: Ask them to delete it and tell a trusted adult if needed
Post a worse one of them
scenarios.why: You are allowed to say no. Ask politely, and get help if they refuse.

intro: School App-1 is a nine-module student companion for everyday school life. You build it yourself, one screen at a time: a welcome page, a homework tracker, a timetable, reminders, a daily quiz, a study helper, a badge board, a digital library and a cyber-safety check.
goals: Build a complete, working mobile app starting from an empty phone screen.
Learn how apps are put together: screens, components, actions and saved data.
Practise reading and writing simple commands, and fixing mistakes.
Finish with an app you can package and publish to Google Play.
studentWill: Drag and drop components and edit their properties.
Type simple commands to add, change and connect things.
Save and show data such as homework, lessons and reminders.
Test each module by running it like a real user.
Choose your own colours and wording to make the app yours.
